fine_trace.note: Each @PG header line parsed from attacker-controlled SAM input increments npg_end, adding the PG index as a potential chain-end candidate.
When a PG line has a PP tag pointing to an already-seen PG, that PG is removed from the npg_end candidate list, decrementing npg_end.

fine_trace.code: for (i = 0; i < hrecs->npg_end; i++) { if (hrecs->pg_end[i] == p_id) { memmove(...); hrecs->npg_end--; } }
fine_trace.note: The removal loop removes at most one occurrence of p_id; if the PP target appears multiple times in pg_end (e.g. via duplicate PG IDs), stale entries remain, keeping npg_end larger than the number of distinct PG lines.

fine_trace.code: hrecs->npg_end_alloc = hrecs->npg; new_pg_end = realloc(hrecs->pg_end, hrecs->npg * sizeof(*new_pg_end));
fine_trace.note: sam_hdr_link_pg reallocates pg_end to exactly npg entries, shrinking the array to the current PG count while npg_end (the old count) is left unchanged.
A PG line with a PP tag referencing a missing program causes ret=-1 and skips linking; the PG keeps chain_size 0 and pg_end[i] stays i, so it never contributes to j.

fine_trace.code: for (i = j = 0; i < hrecs->npg; i++) { if (hrecs->pg_end[i] != -1 && chain_size[i] > 0) hrecs->pg_end[j++] = hrecs->pg_end[i]; }
fine_trace.note: When every PG either has no PP or a PP to a missing program, chain_size[i]==0 for all i, so j stays 0 and no chain end is selected.
With j==0 and old npg_end exceeding npg (because stale duplicate entries were never removed), pg_end[npg_end-1] reads past the npg-entry array, causing the heap-buffer-overflow READ.
